admission.justification: Keeping only on key steps and never dropping within a comparison were weighed and rejected, and every new way to select a subject has to be placed on one side of the line between a row of the tree and everything else.

alternatives.option: Any selection of a row the tree already shows keeps the tree, by key or by click, so a click and `j`/`k` stay the same selection; choosing a subject from outside the tree (catalogue, marker, "All source changes"), a refresh or a new comparison starts fresh.
alternatives.reason: The developer chose it (D36: "Clicks in the tree keep too") and accepted that a click on a family row no longer narrows the tree to that family.

alternatives.option: Only key steps keep the tree.
alternatives.reason: It leaves the click case of the acceptance run, and a click and `j`/`k` would no longer be the same selection.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The ruling that `j` and a tap are the same selection is withdrawn, or the developer asks that a click on a family row narrows the tree to that family again.
A requirement admits a separate control that resets the tree.

consequences: A selection starts the tree afresh unless its caller says it is the selection of a row of the tree, so a new entry point is an outside selection by default.
While the tree holds a kept family, the catalogue lists a row for every family the tree shows, as the way back to one family.
A click on a family row keeps the other families in the tree.
context: Once the tree keeps rows of earlier subjects, something has to say which selections keep them and which drop them. An earlier ruling of this master holds that `j` and a tap are the same selection, and the acceptance run that found the problem also showed it for a click on a family row.
